disclosure: Three AI-agent construction streams, integrated by the main agent. Counts establish exploration coverage only. Exact-string duplicate checking is not semantic independence. No prior-art courts or new searches during this phase.
validation: Structural fields, original component references, counts and paused-input hashes. Causal closure and substantive differences require editorial inspection.

scale_transitions.working_name: Care independence becomes an observation-network state
scale_transitions.unit_of_adoption: Recipients using routine automated care in a specified local support network
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Independent need-witness overlap and reclaimable-support coverage
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Positive success-to-withdrawal feedback can remove a connected corroboration path; total care success or visiting hours need not reveal the cut.
assumptions: Support allocation responds to recorded success.
Witness contexts overlap nonuniformly.
Novel needs require independent substantiation.

stages.conditional_dynamics: One recipient may gain privacy and prompt care; independent family/clinical witnesses usually remain. Measure what the local intervention actually removes.
With 100 recipients sharing visiting staff, success-driven hour reductions can selectively remove overlaps. Test topology at fixed total hours rather than infer a macro loss from count.
Use 10% as a probe for where first witness gaps appear; whether any gap exists depends on which recipients and links adopt.
At the illustrative middle probe, connected corroboration may persist or split. The candidate threshold is a specific context-sharing cut, not 50% itself.
A high-share probe may leave rare needs documented mainly through the aid; alternatively shared assistants can improve witness coordination and add independent observation.
Provider success can influence the human-observation services suppliers keep viable; no single provider controls the entire witness network.
A public entitlement rule using supported independence can make local witness loss an assessment-wide condition; independent reassessment can counteract it.
Shared assessment templates can transmit the dependency across jurisdictions, but independent local testimony rules can keep the systems separable. Global uniformity is not assumed.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: At equal total observation hours, adoption concentrated on overlap bridges produces a larger support-reclaimability loss than dispersed adoption.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same network reconfiguration can remove intrusive cross-context surveillance while keeping recipient-chosen independent support.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: At matched hours and entitlements, bridge removal versus nonbridge removal does not change independent need substantiation.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

scale_transitions.working_name: Junior substitution becomes sector-level expert reproduction
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Teacher reproduction ratio and minimum viable novice-ladder coverage
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Firm replacement and missing intermediate case bands can push a training cohort below replenishment even while current senior workload rises.
assumptions: Experts require a graded supervised sequence.
Some explanation capacity is congestible.
Routine margins finance training organizations.

stages.conditional_dynamics: One organization can borrow training/expertise from others; current output gains need not reduce sector supply.
A hundred firms can all rely on the same external apprenticeship providers. Map who finances and supplies each prerequisite band.
The 10% probe tests whether shared training institutions still have sufficient case volume; it is not a presumed critical fraction.
At 50%, loss of an indispensable intermediate band can bind before senior experts retire, or a funded commons can sustain it. Observe the ladder, not share alone.
At 90%, apparently abundant seniors may mask missing entrant cohorts; common explanations can instead scale successfully if genuinely reusable.
Routine price competition may select organizations that omit training unless future expert production is purchased.
Procurement or public training can internalize future supply, changing the reproduction rate without reducing useful automation.
Cross-border movement may relocate mentors rather than create them; simultaneous dependence on the same explanation institutions can become global, or distributed case commons can add redundancy.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: Two sectors with the same automation share and current experts diverge after one cohort lag if only one preserves the intermediate learning sequence.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: Selection rewarded for transferable expertise spreads better teaching institutions and increases independently usable reserve.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Preserving the claimed indispensable band changes neither cohort completion nor future articulating expert supply.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

scale_transitions.working_name: Policy-specific measurement becomes a comparative observability regime
scale_transitions.unit_of_adoption: Evaluators using deployment-dependent evidence to allocate trials and calibration
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Comparative observability debt and viable independent contrast paths
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Trial concentration improves one policy's local fidelity while losing support that distinguishes alternatives and environment changes; the boundary is loss of informative comparison paths.
assumptions: Finite trials and calibration queries.
Nonidentical policy response support.
Later diagnosis requires some independent variation.

stages.conditional_dynamics: An evaluator can improve one policy's simulator and still retain external comparisons.
A hundred evaluators may independently favor the same legible policy and draw from the same calibration support; count distinct response regimes, not organizations.
A 10% probe tests whether rare alternative regimes still receive enough trials to remain measurable.
The 50% probe could produce positive shared learning or support loss; identify whether calibration transfers across policies.
At 90%, formerly available alternative procedures may no longer run; perfect local estimates can coexist with unknown comparative effects.
Observed rank allocates trials and customers, which finances further local calibration; a shared independent audition reserve can reverse concentration.
Public evaluation schemas may standardize the comparison support or accidentally canonize one policy's deployment regime.
Common benchmarks can share valid corrections worldwide but also spread the same missing contrasts; preserve independent regimes rather than require national/vendor diversity alone.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: At unchanged favored-policy accuracy, maintaining a small running alternative predicts better post-shift causal attribution than keeping a large frozen historical control.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same shared concentration reduces uncertainty rapidly where mechanisms are stable and calibration generalizes.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Removing the only informative alternative path leaves post-shift model/environment attribution equally identifiable.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

scale_transitions.working_name: Optional fast representation becomes the transaction clock
scale_transitions.unit_of_adoption: Counterparties adapting deadlines and recognition to agent-mediated transactions
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Unaided participation region under recognition and response constraints
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Delegated volume funds integration; integration changes binding-status defaults and response windows; lower unaided throughput then increases delegated volume.
assumptions: Counterparties adapt windows to prevailing speed.
Integration is demand-financed.
Some legitimate humans need longer information/recognition intervals.

stages.conditional_dynamics: One principal benefits from fast representation without changing the shared clock.
A hundred participants can finance a local integration norm; test whether counterpart deadlines actually react.
The 10% probe may have no institutional effect or matter if adopters dominate key transactions; share alone is insufficient.
At 50%, the relevant nonlinear event is unaided response time crossing the allowed interval, not majority status itself.
At 90%, declining agent use may still be viable with public recognition/fixed windows or effectively infeasible under speed-responsive defaults.
Competition can induce recognition and timing norms no individual grant authorized as universal participation conditions.
Public services can preserve inclusive clocks and provisional-status acknowledgment, or carry the market norm into basic access.
Interoperability can spread fast participation rules across borders, but heterogeneous clocks and human intermediaries can preserve plural access.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: At identical adoption and agent quality, speed-adaptive deadlines shrink unaided participation more than fixed clocks; initial grants do not need to expand.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same representation network can include people who cannot attend synchronous interactions and preserve useful options.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: With measured response-time requirements, deadline compression has no effect on unaided throughput or further adoption.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

scale_transitions.working_name: Fewer disputes becomes less independent dispute capacity
scale_transitions.unit_of_adoption: Institutions tying objection staffing and admission rules to recorded case volume
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Contestability reserve and merit-conditioned hearing access
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Successful closure lowers funded review stock; cheaper preparation increases arrivals elsewhere; documentary prerequisites ration a scarce complement and suppress observations of rare errors.
assumptions: Complaint volume finances at least some independent review.
Complex review requires maintained expertise.
Prerequisite burdens affect low-resource claims differently.

stages.conditional_dynamics: An institution can close a case efficiently while drawing independent review from the surrounding professional network.
A hundred institutions can all reduce local dispute staff and depend on the same volunteer or expert pool.
At the 10% probe, pools may absorb demand; test complementary preparation savings against added substantive-review arrivals.
At 50%, a minimum viable review-role threshold may bind if routine volume no longer sustains it; no percentage is presumed causal.
At 90%, few admitted complaints can reflect excellent outcomes or low contestability. Independent wrong-case sampling distinguishes them.
Competition on completion metrics can favor institutions whose formal rigor excludes costly claims before counting them.
A guaranteed independent appeal reserve can make low complaint rates genuinely informative again without undoing reliable closure.
Shared review platforms can pool scarce expertise or synchronize the same exclusionary prerequisites; cross-system error sampling matters more than nominal forum count.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: At equal initial accuracy and complaint reduction, protected review stock yields faster rare-error remedy than volume-indexed staffing.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same capacity adaptation can redirect review from repetitive harassment toward serious harms if proof support tracks merit.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Shrinking review stock and raising prerequisites do not alter independently sampled meritorious error access.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

scale_transitions.working_name: Repeated switching grows a portable interpretation commons
scale_transitions.unit_of_adoption: Users and institutions reviewing informative disagreements during provider handovers
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Switch-derived constraint capital and independently articulated compatibility reach
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Provider disagreement teaches explicit constraints; public or user-controlled reuse lowers later switching costs; more viable switches create more informative disagreement, provided the constraints transfer.
assumptions: Handover disagreements reveal relevant distinctions.
Review is bounded and voluntary.
Counterparties accept independently grounded constraints.

stages.conditional_dynamics: One person pays an initial review cost and learns constraints that improve their next transfer.
A hundred consenting users can contribute distinct failure structures without pooling intimate biography; useful constraints may become reusable.
At 10%, a few bridge tests can connect compatible providers, or incompatible private terms can prevent any external benefit.
At 50%, tested interpretation paths may cover a connected switching region; the relevant threshold is accepted constraint connectivity, not adoption share.
At 90%, a shared constraint commons can lower exit costs despite high agent reliance; if one explanation hub monopolizes interpretation, the positive loop becomes a new articulation dependency.
Competition can shift from holding private histories to honoring portable tests while preserving diverse internal ontologies.
Public verification can fund rare legitimate compatibility paths private pairs would not buy, without deciding local legitimacy.
Cross-institution constraint tests can support plural interpretation and resilient exit, provided they do not erase claimant sets or become compulsory single-source certification.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: Initial transfer failures followed by reviewed constraints predict lower later switching costs than initially seamless opaque transfers, at matched total service quality.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: This is a beneficial branch of the same disagreement/learning/switching loop; it expands portable competence rather than merely reducing an adverse effect.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Useful independently accepted constraints learned during switching produce no later transfer improvement.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

scale_transitions.name: Certificate demand becomes infrastructural recognition
scale_transitions.population_definition: Users and providers of one connected professional-service/essential-transaction network; profession percentages are exposure probes, not critical fractions.

stages.mechanism: A certificate lowers one household's transfer rejection; there may be no meaningful recognition-investment feedback yet.
stages.nonlinearity: A single essential counterparty can still make affordability discrete; this is a local bundle constraint.

stages.mechanism: Certificate fees can collectively finance one adapter or issuer agreement that no user could fund alone.
stages.nonlinearity: Lumpy adapter cost makes pooled demand qualitatively different from 100 independent imports.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether scattered certificate demand reaches a financing floor or remains confined to compatible clients.
stages.nonlinearity: No tipping assumed at 10%; new edges require institution-specific minimum investment.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether counterparties begin treating the recognized certificate as the ordinary transaction route.
stages.nonlinearity: If default recognition changes, unaided affordability depends on the joint essential bundle, not average discounts.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether rare independent routes retain sufficient transaction volume to maintain recognition adapters.
stages.nonlinearity: A route can disappear when maintenance demand falls below its cost even with remaining unaided users.

stages.mechanism: Certificate demand and recognition coverage can form a funded network regime affecting entry and usable substitutes.
stages.nonlinearity: A recognition graph cut can remove many feasible trades at once; provider counts alone do not describe it.

stages.mechanism: If public entitlements recognize the certificate, identity/standing policy can alter essential access and levy-like demand.
stages.nonlinearity: This depends on actual public recognition rules; it is not a claim of state authority automatically arising from fees.

stages.mechanism: Cross-border issuer agreements can turn domestic cuts into international recognition bottlenecks or plural bridges.
stages.nonlinearity: Different guarantee/jurisdiction rules can prevent scaling or create new path-level thresholds.

scale_transitions.candidate_critical_condition: Certificate-funded adapter coverage makes the relevant essential bundle unaffordable outside recognized paths, or removes the last independent recognition path; institution/resource dependent.
scale_transitions.beneficial_branch: Investment expands plural issuers and manual recognition, making the same pooled-demand transition inclusive.
scale_transitions.measurement: Affordable anchor-free essential bundles and recognized alternative paths at each exposure probe.
scale_transitions.falsifier: Rising penetration funds only plural independent recognition and leaves anchor-free bundle affordability unchanged.

scale_transitions.name: Routine procurement selects the recovery-production ecology
scale_transitions.population_definition: Purchasers and training organizations within a professional sector; exposure percentages refer to routine work procured under insured-output criteria.

stages.mechanism: A purchaser chooses cheap insured routine service; its decision does not alone establish sector training decline.
stages.nonlinearity: One rare recovery need may depend on expertise paid for elsewhere.

stages.mechanism: Common contract preferences can affect whether a local apprenticeship-bearing organization remains viable.
stages.nonlinearity: Organization closure removes a teaching complement that cannot be divided into 100 small price effects.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether lost contracts reduce marginal teaching capacity or are absorbed by other firms.
stages.nonlinearity: No critical 10% claim; replacement capacity and firm cash-flow floors determine consequences.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether case distribution loses an intermediate learning rung even while total human exception work rises.
stages.nonlinearity: Prerequisite gaps block progression despite equal aggregate task hours.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether rare independent training routes have enough mentor/case flow to replenish retiring expertise.
stages.nonlinearity: Cohort replenishment can fail below a complementarity floor; no 90% threshold is asserted.

stages.mechanism: Purchasers optimize routine output and monetary readiness while no buyer pays for collectively needed standby judgment.
stages.nonlinearity: The recovery skill supply is produced before common failure, not created by cash claims during it.

stages.mechanism: If public sectors rely on the same profession, private procurement composition can alter public emergency/restoration capacity.
stages.nonlinearity: Mandated reserve funding or public teaching can break the transition; private market loss need not determine state capacity.

stages.mechanism: Cross-border outsourcing can spread common demand onto the same mentors and insurance-funded substitutes.
stages.nonlinearity: Global diversification of firms may still concentrate the graded teaching ecology; portability and migration may instead replenish it.

scale_transitions.candidate_critical_condition: Graded case/mentor replenishment falls below expert attrition while monetary indemnity substitutes for actual recovery provision; no critical adoption fraction supplied.
scale_transitions.beneficial_branch: Insurance buys tested judgment and transferable teaching, so larger pooled demand reproduces expertise rather than only insures its absence.
scale_transitions.measurement: Deliverable independent recovery judgment, novice progression and between-firm training weights, not indemnity totals alone.
scale_transitions.falsifier: Output/insurance procurement leaves graded training and mentor replenishment at or above attrition throughout the probes.

scale_transitions.name: Individual independence reporting becomes public reserve dependence
scale_transitions.population_definition: Care recipients/institutions using assisted performance for eligibility; percentages refer to the care profession's served caseload under that rule.

stages.mechanism: Supported assessment can be valid for the sampled task yet miss a person's residual needs.
stages.nonlinearity: An individual's eligibility discontinuity can occur at a scoring boundary but says nothing about public capacity.

stages.mechanism: Case selection can concentrate unsampled needs in families or one local emergency team.
stages.nonlinearity: Overlap of residual need and common alarms changes peak demand independently of mean need.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether excluded needs are absorbed by ordinary independent services.
stages.nonlinearity: 10% is only a probe; substitute capacity may be ample or already fragile.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether renewed success evidence resets the normal independence baseline across institutions.
stages.nonlinearity: Changing the eligibility denominator can make a formerly temporary aid practically necessary.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether unsampled needs have any independently funded ordinary route left.
stages.nonlinearity: Loss of a last alternative route is distinct from a gradual increase in assisted task success.

stages.mechanism: Renewal favors manageable cohorts, while hidden residual needs seek services outside measured programs.
stages.nonlinearity: Selection changes the remaining need distribution rather than simply its average severity.

stages.mechanism: Synchronized escalation can exhaust public responders and displace nonusers who were never assessed by the agents.
stages.nonlinearity: Peak residual demand above reserve K creates public access loss; exact K is local and variable.

stages.mechanism: Shared eligibility/alert templates can correlate residual demand across care systems, subject to different public reserves.
stages.nonlinearity: Shared templates do not guarantee common crises; independent full-population follow-up and response coordination can break coupling.

scale_transitions.candidate_critical_condition: Excluded residual needs persist and synchronized escalation exceeds deliverable reserve K; eligibility feedback also requires renewal to ignore full-population follow-up.
scale_transitions.beneficial_branch: Real capability gains and independent excluded-need tracking let the same adoption free ordinary/public care rather than silently transfer demand.
scale_transitions.measurement: Common-denominator need, excluded-need follow-up and tail nonuser response delay at each probe.
scale_transitions.falsifier: Independent follow-up shows total residual need declining and peak reserve demand remaining within capacity despite the purported denominator effect.

scale_transitions.name: Embodied maintenance selection reshapes planning evidence
scale_transitions.population_definition: Occupants and public-space robot deployments; profession probes refer to logistics/maintenance operators using low-tuning standard etiquette.

stages.mechanism: A standard gesture or holding pattern changes one encounter; it need not displace any cultural practice.
stages.nonlinearity: The individual preference remains separable from fleet prevalence.

stages.mechanism: Repeated inexpensive deployments can replace local gestures and occupy a shared courtyard or waiting area.
stages.nonlinearity: Stationary uses compete for shared space; summed polite encounter scores omit that resource.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether tuning savings alter replacement while locally preferred behavior remains easy to procure.
stages.nonlinearity: No percentage threshold; maintenance budgets and reusable tuning determine survival.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether planners' observed travel now mostly comes from machine-compatible routes.
stages.nonlinearity: Observation selection can change the represented city even while true local preferences remain fixed.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether displaced stationary activities still have any recognized channel into procurement evidence.
stages.nonlinearity: The loss of a last evidence path is more consequential than the remaining number of nonusers.

stages.mechanism: Maintenance cost selects fleets, and fleet-shaped observed use selects future contracts and street demand.
stages.nonlinearity: The two selection systems reinforce; low cost and local preference may diverge.

stages.mechanism: Public budgets and spatial rules can entrench the machine-compatible observation sample.
stages.nonlinearity: Independent public-space standing or protected stationary-use evidence can reverse the selection.

stages.mechanism: Exported low-tuning fleets/templates can reproduce a standardized observation boundary across cities.
stages.nonlinearity: Local maintenance and rights rules may prevent transfer; global textual localization is not evidence of embodied equivalence.

scale_transitions.candidate_critical_condition: Locally meaningful use loses its last independent recognized evidence path while tuning funding responds to observed movement, not latent preference.
scale_transitions.beneficial_branch: Reusable local tuning and genuinely spare waiting areas make the same maintenance/use feedback affordable and culturally legible.
scale_transitions.measurement: Preferred gestures and stationary uses represented in planning/procurement versus their independent prevalence.
scale_transitions.falsifier: Independent stationary-use evidence and local tuning persist, preventing the predicted evidence-depletion return.

scale_transitions.name: Competitive entry grows a shared recognition cut
scale_transitions.population_definition: Providers and counterparties in one professional service market; percentages describe transactions exposed to incompatible attestation entry.

stages.mechanism: One switch can succeed through an anchor credential; no market selection result follows.
stages.nonlinearity: Export success differs from recognition of actual post-switch obligations.

stages.mechanism: Transfer demand can make anchor certification viable and fund common adapters.
stages.nonlinearity: A lumpy recognition service can turn scattered choices into a shared route.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether new formats add genuinely independent paths or only anchor-routed options.
stages.nonlinearity: No 10% critical fraction; adapter budgets and graph topology determine reachability.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether counterparties economize by relying on the anchor rather than maintaining every provider adapter.
stages.nonlinearity: Removing one adapter can disconnect a large recognition component despite unchanged provider count.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether independent issuer paths remain commercially maintained for uncommon relationships.
stages.nonlinearity: Sparse route maintenance can disappear even though nominal substitutes are numerous.

stages.mechanism: Certificate demand helps entry, while entry adds the incompatible obligations that grow certificate demand.
stages.nonlinearity: This is the added endogenous financing return, not merely the known fact that more providers can mean less usable exit.

stages.mechanism: If public/professional licenses recognize the anchor, entry and essential standing become coupled.
stages.nonlinearity: Independent public recognition can break dependence without standardizing every internal ontology.

stages.mechanism: International recognition chains can extend an anchor cut or create genuine redundancy across issuers.
stages.nonlinearity: Cross-border legitimacy is not implied by technical certificate verification.

scale_transitions.candidate_critical_condition: All essential counterpart recognition paths traverse a funded anchor while adapter budgets cannot preserve alternative attestations; graph/resource dependent.
scale_transitions.beneficial_branch: Plural interchangeable issuers use demand-financed certificates to connect previously isolated markets and sustain independent paths.
scale_transitions.measurement: Actual completed anchor-free replacement transactions and independent recognition connectivity.
scale_transitions.falsifier: Entry consistently increases anchor-free essential recognition paths even under the specified adapter budget.

scale_transitions.name: Relationship transitions reproduce public human capability
scale_transitions.population_definition: Users, voluntary repair helpers and transition-care professionals; percentages describe support episodes routed through teachable public/communal programs.

stages.mechanism: A teachable repair episode can create one new skill or helpful tie; it may instead impose burden.
stages.nonlinearity: Learning occurs only if the task is genuinely teachable and the helper can decline.

stages.mechanism: Repeated cases can supply enough shared distinctions to sustain a local teaching/support group.
stages.nonlinearity: Reusable knowledge changes marginal transition cost rather than merely adding volunteer hours.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether retained skills offset attrition and whether helpers remain voluntary.
stages.nonlinearity: No 10% threshold; replenishment depends on case diversity, teachability and time.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether institutions recognize transition support as a stable public competence independent of machine status.
stages.nonlinearity: Recognition can unlock resources and apprenticeships; it can also harden an unpaid office if not bounded.

stages.mechanism: Probe whether the repertoire stays diverse enough for uncommon needs instead of selecting only cheap teachable transitions.
stages.nonlinearity: High coverage may concentrate evidence and hide hard cases; beneficial scaling is not assumed.

stages.mechanism: Portable transition expertise lowers replacement cost and can support providers without binding care to one stack.
stages.nonlinearity: Learning spillovers change supply of substitutes, not just present user satisfaction.

stages.mechanism: Reliable inclusive transitions can attract activity and justify resources that reproduce the public program.
stages.nonlinearity: The loop closes only if resource returns actually fund human capability rather than other objectives.

stages.mechanism: Portable case/negative-constraint knowledge can circulate while local consent and claimant rules remain plural.
stages.nonlinearity: Knowledge portability can spread capability without identical culture; copying templates alone may lose local standing.

scale_transitions.candidate_critical_condition: Portable skill and resource replenishment exceed helper attrition and operating burden while participation remains voluntary; no universal adoption fraction.
scale_transitions.beneficial_branch: The principal branch is beneficial social reproduction: more transitions produce more independent capability and lower later external burden.
scale_transitions.measurement: Retained transferable expertise, family burden, real decline routes and independent completed handovers.
scale_transitions.falsifier: Scaling consumes volunteers without portable learning or resource replenishment, so transition costs do not decline.

scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Unsettled mandate-hours, arrival burst covariance and jointly available qualified disposition capacity.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: An initially finite synchronized stopping burst can become self-sustaining if delayed release creates additional reconciliation arrivals faster than dispositions remove them. The relevant boundary is state-dependent arrival work versus disposition capacity, not adoption percentage.
assumptions: Stops are honored locally.
Several mandates share restoration and assessment pools.
Waiting counterparties can create additional genuine reconciliation work.
At large institutional scope, shared settlement links must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

stages.conditional_prediction: One stop is normally settled if its work fits available reserve; the formal stop and recognized release may still differ.
stages.measurement: Record local stop time, residual obligations and disposition-hours.

stages.conditional_prediction: A common disturbance can synchronize 100 claims even if average daily workload is low; queue tail rises when their shared work exhausts burst reserve.
stages.measurement: Compare independent versus common-mode stop notifications, holding total claim work fixed.

stages.conditional_prediction: If adopters cluster on one settlement pool, this probe can cross saturation earlier than a uniformly dispersed 50% probe; no particular fraction is critical.
stages.measurement: Measure pool-specific simultaneous work and the additional reliance-generated arrival rate.

stages.conditional_prediction: If use-based funding has reduced reserve, a shared wave can enter a persistent arrears regime; equal nominal staffing need not imply equal unreserved capacity.
stages.measurement: Measure precommitted staffing separately from genuinely available disposition capacity.

stages.conditional_prediction: If independent substitute channels have disappeared, stopping can still be immediate locally while common recognized release remains slow; independently funded substitutes would avoid this.
stages.measurement: Measure substitute-path availability and recognized-release tail latency.

stages.conditional_prediction: A common clearing or recognition institution can couple otherwise competing providers' stop waves; independent clearing pools can uncouple them.
stages.measurement: Trace cross-provider residual obligations entering the same queue.

stages.conditional_prediction: Publicly mandated settlement deadlines can create a second synchronized peak or fund a protective disposition reserve, depending on policy.
stages.measurement: Compare calendar clustering and legally funded reserve rather than inferring an effect of regulation alone.

stages.conditional_prediction: Cross-jurisdiction recognition of unsettled mandates can propagate workload only along actual shared obligations; fragmented systems may instead bound the cascade.
stages.measurement: Measure the connected residual-obligation graph and work crossing jurisdictional interfaces.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same pooled settlement concentrates expertise and quickly clears synchronized stops when reserve scales with burst work and waiting does not generate uncontrolled new claims.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Same stop count, local permissions, total original work and staffing, but independent arrival schedules and a separate bounded residual-reliance queue.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: At verified shared capacity and endogenous reconciliation, increased arrival synchronization produces no persistent arrears or tail-release difference.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: Additional work may be bounded, clearing may automate safely, counterparties may waive reliance; no queue law or inevitable global cascade is asserted.

scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Independent counterparty recognition path count, smallest recognition cut and certifier share, measured separately from provider share.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Format proliferation draws on fixed adapter resources. A common certifier lowers local costs; adoption reduces maintenance of alternative paths. The discontinuity occurs when loss of the final independent proof path makes the certifier a necessary cut.
assumptions: Attestation formats are not automatically interoperable.
Counterparties maintain proof paths at positive cost.
Common certification can displace rather than merely supplement alternate maintenance.

stages.conditional_prediction: A single provider-to-counterparty proof path can be checked directly; certification need not be necessary.
stages.measurement: Observe actual accepted proofs and maintenance cost.

stages.conditional_prediction: One hundred providers may create many compatibility demands, but a common open proof format can keep adapter work low.
stages.measurement: Count distinct required transformations, not provider logos.

stages.conditional_prediction: An adopter cluster may choose a common certifier to conserve interpretation work; gate dependence remains contingent on alternative proof maintenance.
stages.measurement: Measure alternative proof acceptance before and after common certification.

stages.conditional_prediction: If resources follow certified transaction volume, alternate maintenance can fall below viability even while provider competition increases.
stages.measurement: Measure adapter funding, accepted alternate paths and provider versus certifier concentration.

stages.conditional_prediction: Loss of the last non-certifier path makes the gate necessary under the stipulated counterparty rule; 90% alone does not establish that loss.
stages.measurement: Attempt a valid transfer with the certifier unavailable.

stages.conditional_prediction: Entrants can competitively price service while all require the same recognition gate, shifting the bottleneck from service provision to standing.
stages.measurement: Compare provider switching with gate switching under fixed guarantees.

stages.conditional_prediction: Procurement or official acceptance can make one certification sufficient, exclusive, or merely optional; only exclusivity or path displacement creates the proposed cut.
stages.measurement: Inspect accepted proof alternatives and funded interoperability routes.

stages.conditional_prediction: Cross-border mutual recognition can either diversify proofs or align institutions on one inherited gate; the last-path test remains decisive.
stages.measurement: Construct the actual transnational proof graph and identify independent accepted routes.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same common certification reduces repeated interpretation and enables useful provider entry when multiple independent accepted proof routes remain viable.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Hold provider count, service quality and transaction volume fixed; vary whether independent adapters receive protected maintenance resources.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: More incompatible provider entry under verified fixed adapter capacity leaves alternate recognition paths intact and certifier dependence unchanged.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: The bottleneck may be a generic standard or ordinary network effect; this exercise asserts only the conditional measurement distinction, not new theoretical priority.

scale_transitions.working_name: Individual skills to extinct recovery complements
scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Number of required recovery classes with an independently available mentor-complement path at the moment of an unannounced shock.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Recovery is a complementary production hypergraph, not the sum of individual skill scores. A last essential class or mentor path can disappear while common-class practice grows. Success-conditioned reduction in mentoring makes the loss persist after hardware or route restoration.
assumptions: Some recovery tasks require multiple distinct skills.
Temporary announced-test help does not guarantee shock-time availability.
Mentor succession requires real class-specific practice.
Large-scale specialization or sharing may preserve complements and must be tested.

stages.conditional_prediction: One person can be individually competent but require an absent complementary helper; self-contained tasks avoid this condition.
stages.measurement: Map required skill combinations for one concrete recovery task.

stages.conditional_prediction: A network of 100 people can borrow rare skills for announced tests, masking local inability during an unannounced disturbance.
stages.measurement: Compare announced borrowing against simultaneous independent local availability.

stages.conditional_prediction: Adoption clustered around one specialist can remove enough ordinary encounters to interrupt succession locally, regardless of total adoption.
stages.measurement: Measure specialist mentoring contacts and local novice progress.

stages.conditional_prediction: Shared rare-class mentors may serve many apparently resilient sites; simultaneous failure can reveal that their advertised coverage was multiply counted.
stages.measurement: Conduct a bounded joint drill with total expert availability held fixed.

stages.conditional_prediction: If the last live mentor path retires, restoring average hours cannot immediately restore the missing complement; retained substitutes prevent the discontinuity.
stages.measurement: Track last-path loss and time to competent successor, not adoption rate itself.

stages.conditional_prediction: Provider-funded drills may assemble mobile expert help whose repeated success lowers each customer's local training budget.
stages.measurement: Record announced support transfers and local successor investment.

stages.conditional_prediction: Certification of aggregate hours can miss class extinction; class-specific apprentice-path requirements can preserve recovery diversity.
stages.measurement: Compare qualification coverage with actual simultaneous complementary performance.

stages.conditional_prediction: International specialization can preserve rare expertise cheaply or expose many sites to one unavailable complement; connectivity and shock independence determine which.
stages.measurement: Map real specialist pools, geographic covariance and transport or communication availability.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same sharing and joint demonstration teach local successors and maintain rare classes when they are used as apprenticeship rather than solely readiness evidence.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Match average skill, total training hours and equipment; protect one independent succession path for every required class.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Loss of an independently verified necessary class path creates no unannounced recovery deficit despite absence of a genuine substitute.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: The relevant complement may be unnecessary, substitutable or remotely available; evidence of an actual critical class is required before claiming any phase boundary.

scale_transitions.working_name: Courteous robot density to inherited access precedence
scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Recoverable manual-route capacity, persistent waiting footprint and the cost/time of reversing accommodation after mandates stop.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Each courteous interaction can be acceptable while aggregate waiting occupation creates temporary accommodation. Repeated accommodation becomes an inherited planning default; once independent route restoration costs exceed continuing accommodation, stopping individual robots no longer restores the earlier access regime.
assumptions: Waiting and yielding use physical space.
Repeated accommodations affect later design or access conventions.
Manual alternatives can decay or be removed.
Human users' observed movement is an incomplete measure of dormant needs.

stages.conditional_prediction: One yielding robot may improve access or impose negligible delay; a precedent need not form.
stages.measurement: Observe yielding, waiting footprint and displaced uses.

stages.conditional_prediction: Dense courteous waiting can exhaust a shared approach even with zero local etiquette violations.
stages.measurement: Measure concurrent stationary footprint and access, not collision count.

stages.conditional_prediction: A clustered installation can induce a temporary route concession before a uniformly dispersed higher-adoption setting.
stages.measurement: Compare equal robot counts with clustered and dispersed staging.

stages.conditional_prediction: Repeated concessions can become routine access expectations; maintenance decisions may stop protecting the old manual alternative.
stages.measurement: Record precedence changes, old-route maintenance and dormant users' claims.

stages.conditional_prediction: If restoring independent access exceeds the practical remedy horizon, stopping many robots leaves inherited redesign in place.
stages.measurement: Test physical route usability and restoration delay after simulated stop.

stages.conditional_prediction: Standard staging practices across suppliers can reproduce occupation even when customers switch providers.
stages.measurement: Measure supplier-independent waiting geometry and recognized access rules.

stages.conditional_prediction: Public access rules can preserve manual routes or ratify inherited accommodation; ordinary microgrants alone do not decide legitimacy.
stages.measurement: Measure protected independent access and the provenance of changed public defaults.

stages.conditional_prediction: Shared infrastructure standards can export staging conventions across cities, but local geometry and access law may prevent the same transition.
stages.measurement: Compare matched sites adopting the convention with independently protected routes.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same courteous repetition establishes reliable coordination and accessible shared spaces when staging and redesign preserve human alternatives and dormant needs.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Keep robot tasks, yielding compliance and movement volume fixed; constrain stationary staging footprints and preserve an independently usable route.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Repeated accommodation and documented manual-route decay do not increase reversal cost or persistent access precedence after stopping.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: Occupation need not harm anyone; redesign may genuinely improve access. The claimed variable is reversibility of alternatives, not a presumption against robots.

scale_transitions.working_name: Proposal output to institutional action reach
scale_transitions.probe_levels_not_critical_fractions: 1 and 100 agents, then 10%, 50% and 90% of a potential population N>=10,000, followed by market/state/global institutional probes. These are comparison settings, not asserted thresholds or a necessary historical sequence.
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: External consequence reach of an unchanged proposal interface: resources, decisions or places reachable through accepted counterparty execution rules.
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: External bridges turn proposals into transactions. Those executions create usage evidence that reallocates infrastructure, expanding what later proposals can execute. A change in institutional acceptance or infrastructure capacity—not a larger local permission set—can produce a discontinuous increase in reach.
assumptions: Some counterparties act on provisional outputs.
Planning responds to realized use.
Added infrastructure actually extends executable outcomes.
All larger-scale institutional links are prospective models, not assertions of actual authority.

stages.conditional_prediction: One proposal can become an action when one counterparty has an execution bridge; without a bridge it remains advice.
stages.measurement: Trace a proposal to a verified external state change.

stages.conditional_prediction: Repeated execution may produce a stable demand signal while local proposal permissions remain fixed.
stages.measurement: Compare accepted proposal outputs and external transactions under the same interface.

stages.conditional_prediction: If accepted outputs are concentrated on one route or service, planners may cross an allocation threshold at this probe or another level.
stages.measurement: Identify the actual planning decision rule and its observed input.

stages.conditional_prediction: Allocation toward adapted use can increase executable reach and make independent channels less convenient, feeding further execution.
stages.measurement: Measure before/after physical capacity and availability of non-bridge routes.

stages.conditional_prediction: If external institutions now treat the output as routine, the same local proposal can affect a wider set of consequences than at entry; this is not automatically illegitimate.
stages.measurement: Hold local scope constant and measure the reachable external outcome set.

stages.conditional_prediction: Competing providers may share external execution institutions, so local switching changes authorship but not the expanded action channel.
stages.measurement: Compare provider-specific scope with common counterparty execution defaults.

stages.conditional_prediction: Official planning or acceptance can enlarge or limit proposal consequence reach; provenance of the public decision distinguishes authorized collective adaptation from drift.
stages.measurement: Record allocation decisions, accountability and explicit public authorization separately.

stages.conditional_prediction: Interoperable execution bridges can extend reach across jurisdictions, but absent acceptance or physical capacity breaks propagation.
stages.measurement: Test accepted cross-border transformations and the external resources actually reachable.

scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same execution-and-planning feedback builds useful infrastructure where accepted proposals reveal legitimate unmet needs and public allocation preserves meaningful independent channels.
scale_transitions.neutral_control: Hold proposal outputs and local permission sets fixed; compare external execution without usage-responsive infrastructure allocation against the coupled condition.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: Verified bridge execution and responsive planning change no external reachable outcomes under the fixed local interface.
scale_transitions.uncertainty: Allocation may reflect prior demand rather than agent-induced demand; macro reach is not necessarily coercive, harmful, unauthorized or commercially malicious.
